page: Amazon Web Services m7gd.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by AWS Graviton3 processors utilizing the 64-bit ARM64 architecture. It features 64 dedicated physical cores and 64 vCPUs based on the Neoverse-V1 microarchitecture running at 2.6 GHz, with 1.0 thread per core. The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It includes 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps under the Nitro hypervisor.

In benchmark evaluations, the m7gd.16xlarge demonstrates strong multi-core performance, highlighted by a stress-ng multi-core score of 97895.22 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 20645.0. Its memory subsystem is highly efficient, achieving top-tier results in Passmark memory testing and strong read-only memory bandwidth of 253.41 GB/sec for large blocks. Software compilation via Clang is a notable strength, placing in the top tier of tested hardware. Database and key-value store operations are also highly performant, with Redis SET operations reaching 102.0 million operations per second and Passmark database operations showing strong throughput.

While multi-threaded and memory-intensive workloads excel, single-core performance remains average, as shown by stress-ng and Geekbench single-core metrics. Additionally, LLM text generation performance for small models is relatively weak at 61.82 tokens per second, though medium model text generation is strong. Given the combination of 3800 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, high memory bandwidth, and balanced compute resources, this instance is highly suited for database hosting, static web serving, software compilation pipelines, and general-purpose containerized workloads.
